title: Typing With Backspaces

concept.title: The stack is the text typed so far
body: A `#` means "backspace": it erases the last typed letter, if there is one. Simulate typing with a stack that holds the text: a letter is **pushed**, a `#` **pops** the top (nothing happens on an empty stack). At the end the stack is the final text.
To compare two typed words, compare the two stacks. (There is also a solution that walks both words from the end in O(1) extra memory; the stack solution is the clearer one to start with.)

statement: Two words are typed into empty text editors. The character `#` means a backspace: it deletes the last letter in the editor, and does nothing if the editor is empty. Print `yes` if both editors end up with the same text, otherwise `no`. Two empty texts are equal.
inputFormat: The first line has the first typed word.
The second line has the second typed word.
constraints: The words contain lowercase letters and the character `#`.

examples.note: The first editor shows c, the second shows b.

hints: Simulate each editor with a stack.
A letter is pushed; a `#` pops the top if the stack is not empty.

starter.python:
s = input().strip()
t = input().strip()

explanation: Each word is typed into a stack: letters are pushed and `#` pops when possible. The words give the same text exactly when the two stacks are equal.
solution.complexity: Time O(n + m), space O(n + m).
